newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Prime unit's owed charges written off.
newsitem.headline: Prime unit's owed charges written off.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Wednesday the government has agreed to write off arrears on sewerage charges owed by consumers to Indah Water Konsortium (IWK).
"We have abolished the arrears owed by consumers and reduced the charge for individuals and own usage under the new formula," the national Bernama news agency quoted Mahathir as saying.
Indah Water is a subsidiary of Prime Utilities Bhd.

Last month, Malaysia ordered IWK to temporarily suspend its billing and collection activities in Kuala Lumpur and five other states effective November 1 pending the outcome of a review of sewerage charges.
IWK was granted the concession to take over the country's sewerage services in April 1994 for 28 years as part of a government privatisation drive.
But consumer complaints about IWK's desludging methods and high charges prompted the government to probe the sewerage firm.
IWK had been charging between two ringgit and 10 ringgit a month for each household.
Bernama did not provide any details on the amount of arrears to be written off or the new charges.
Officials at Prime did not have any comment on the government's statement, but a spokeswoman said more information on the new charges would be released by the housing ministry on Thursday.
Mahathir also said the Cabinet on Wednesday decided that the government would provide IWK with a loan of 450 million ringgit so that it could avoid increasing its sewerage charges.
The government had already given a 475 million ringgit soft loan to the sewerage company to help its operations. IWK runs more than 2,000 treatment plants.
